summary: Sumo Logic ingest sample + cryptographic archive delivery spec for regulatory evidence
description:
Issue summary: Customer (Arcadia Financial Services) requests a one-time, on-demand delivery of a Sumo Logic-compatible ingest sample (24-hour window) plus an auditable encrypted archive and cryptographic manifest for regulatory review. They require field-level mapping to Sumo's ECS-like ingestion fields, a tamper-evident SHA-256 chain over ordered objects, and HSM/ED25519 signature attestation on the manifest.

Impact: Customer cannot complete an external compliance review until they receive the exact ingest samples and a signed archive proving chain-of-custody and non-repudiation. This is blocking their SOC2 audit evidentiary package.

Requested deliverables: 1) A 24-hour sample file (newline-delimited JSON) mapped to Sumo Logic recommended fields with UTC timestamps and tenant-scoped identifiers. 2) Encrypted archive (AES-256-GCM) in S3 with object-lock enabled and retention metadata. 3) A manifest (JSON) listing objects, byte ranges, SHA-256 checksums, ordered sequence number, and a signature block (ed25519 public key and signature). 4) A short verification playbook describing how Arcadia can verify signatures and replay the sample to Sumo Logic ingest.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer requests evidence via account rep on 2026-03-11.
2) Support triages and requests scope and acceptable Sumo field mapping.
3) Support to produce sample export from prod audit-store for tenant arcadia-prod between 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z and 2026-03-01T23:59:59Z.
4) Create encrypted archive with object lock, generate manifest, sign with HSM-attested ed25519 key, deliver presigned S3 URLs to customer and post proof in ticket.

investigation_notes:
Hypothesis: Export pipeline can produce required fields but needs a mapping step to Sumo ECS names (e.g., 'tenant_id' -> 'tenant.id', 'request_id' -> 'request.id', 'user_email' -> 'user.email'). Verified mapping module exists at platform repo, mapping version v2.3.1.
Work performed: Ran export-job export-20260301-ARC-72 in staging to validate field mapping. Found two fields with inconsistent timestamp formats (microseconds vs milliseconds) — normalized to RFC3339 nano with UTC. Confirmed pseudonymization plugin hooks into envelope encryption with customer KMS via kms:encrypt API.
Evidence: staging sample uploaded to s3://redwood-test/arcadia/samples/2026-03-12/sample-100.ndjson (permissioned to arcadia).
Open risks: Need legal sign-off for reversible pseudonymization workflow; ensure customer-side KMS key policy allows decryption by their auditors. Need to coordinate HSM key usage window for signature export to produce attestation log (KMSTOOL audit proof).
resolution:
Workaround/Fix: Support completed a two-part delivery: (A) inline sample: attached the first 100 NDJSON events normalized to Sumo field names and pseudonymized user identifiers (sample provided to customer via secure share). (B) Full 24-hour archive: created export, applied pseudonymization with customer's envelope KMS, encrypted archive uploaded to s3://redwood-evidence/arcadia/exports/2026-03-01/export-20260301-ARC-72.enc, object-lock retention 90 days, presigned GET URL delivered.
Manifest and signature: manifest.json includes ordered object list, byte offsets, SHA-256 checksums, and ed25519 signature using HSM key 'hsm-ed25519-07'. We recorded KMSTOOL audit log entries and a short attestation note (confluence link below).
Delivery notes: Presigned URL and verification playbook sent to customer on 2026-03-13 10:05 UTC. Customer verified signature locally using provided public key and openssl ed25519 verification steps.
Follow-up items: 1) Legal to confirm acceptance of reversible pseudonymization for audit (owner: Legal). 2) Add a small support-runbook for Sumo Logic ingest examples (owner: DevEx). 3) Add SDK helper to produce Sumo ECS crosswalk automatically (owner: Platform Engineering).
